title: The homogeneous core of a prime ideal is a homogeneous prime ideal
statement: Let $R=\bigoplus_{d\ge0}R_d$ be a commutative ring with a nonnegative grading as a $\mathbf Z$-algebra [def-sfb-nonnegative-graded-algebra]: the $R_d$ are additive subgroups, every element has a unique finite sum of components in the $R_d$, $1\in R_0$, and $R_aR_b\subseteq R_{a+b}$. Call an element homogeneous if it belongs to some $R_d$, and an ideal homogeneous if it contains every homogeneous component of each of its elements. Let $\mathfrak p$ be a prime ideal of $R$, meaning a proper ideal such that $ab\in\mathfrak p$ implies $a\in\mathfrak p$ or $b\in\mathfrak p$. Define $\mathfrak p^*$ to be the ideal generated by all homogeneous elements belonging to $\mathfrak p$. Then $\mathfrak p^*$ is a homogeneous prime ideal of $R$ and $\mathfrak p^*\subseteq\mathfrak p$.
